claims.text: The targeted material family is soft-magnetic high-entropy alloys derived from Fe-Co-Ni.
The specific property targeted for improvement is saturation magnetization (Ms).
FeCoNiCr and FeCoNiCrMn are relevant fcc Fe-Co-Ni-derived alloy variants.
These alloys are paramagnetic or weakly ferromagnetic at room temperature.
Local chemical or magnetic short-range order is important in Fe-Co-Ni-Cr alloys.
Adding Mn to FeCoNiCr can produce magnetic frustration by eliminating the energy difference between fcc and hcp structures.
Current first-principles calculations often neglect or underestimate orbital magnetic moments in these alloys.
Neglecting or underestimating orbital moments systematically causes calculated saturation magnetization to exceed experiment.
DFT calculations lacking explicit orbital-moment and thermal-spin-fluctuation treatments overestimate saturation magnetization by 10–30%.
Orbital moments are quenched in an ideal fcc environment.
Local symmetry breaking from chemical disorder and magnetic frustration partially unquenches orbital moments.
Accurate treatment of orbital moments requires explicit spin-orbit coupling together with thermal-spin-fluctuation models.
DLM and fluctuating-medium methods can model longitudinal spin fluctuations over 50–1200 K in fcc CoCrFeMnNi.
Thermal spin fluctuations induce longitudinal magnetic moments in Cr and Ni.
Thermally induced longitudinal moments alter magnetic entropy, internal energy, and total magnetic moment.
Cr moments can align antiferromagnetically relative to their coordination shell and reduce the net magnetic moment.
The interplay of spin-orbit coupling and thermal fluctuations determines the magnitude of the orbital-moment contribution.
Including orbital moments and thermal spin fluctuations will reduce predicted saturation magnetization and bring it closer to experiment.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to BCC HEAs or systems with negligible magnetic interactions.
The orbital-moment magnitude depends on composition, local atomic arrangement, and temperature.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says orbital moments become significant when unquenched, but predicts that explicitly adding their contribution will reduce total saturation magnetization. No antiparallel orbital alignment or other sign-changing mechanism is stated to reconcile a significant added orbital contribution with a lower total moment.
